rules.title: Deomali hilltop: no visitors at night
rules.detail: The Collector barred visitors from 8 pm to 5 am. In September 2026 entry was reported as 5 am to 5 pm, with the hilltop cleared by 8 pm.
rules.applies_to: All visitors, except guests booked in recognised cottages and camps

source.title: Odisha's Koraput admin bans night visit to Deomali hilltop

history.change: Private camping on the hilltop was banned.

source.title: Plastic Banned On Odisha's Deomali; Check Other Restrictions For Tourists

history.change: Collector's order barred visitors from 8 pm to 5 am and banned single-use plastic and unapproved picnics.

source.title: Odisha's Koraput admin bans night visit to Deomali hilltop

history.change: After assaults on tourists, entry was limited to 5 am to 5 pm, trekking stopped after 6 pm, and police and cameras were posted.

source.title: Trekking restricted after 6 PM as Koraput admin beefs up security at Deomali

rules.title: Deomali: last stretch to the top shut for roadworks
rules.detail: In November 2025 the 3.5 kilometre road from Deomali Chhak to the top was closed for construction, with a longer diversion by Semiliguda, Dudhari and Uparakanti. No reopening date found.

source.title: Deomali main road to remain closed for tourists as construction work continues in Odisha's Koraput

rules.title: Deomali: no single-use plastic, no unapproved picnics
rules.detail: Single-use plastic and littering are banned on the hilltop, with a fine reported in the press. Picnics and parties need permission from the administration.

source.title: Plastic Banned On Odisha's Deomali; Check Other Restrictions For Tourists

season.note: The cool dry months from October to February suit both coast and hills; July and August are the wettest months at Puri.

hazards.title: Slippery hill roads to Deomali in the monsoon
hazards.detail: An operator warns that the winding road up from Koraput turns slippery in the rains.

source.title: Deomali Mountain Peak, Koraput - Travel Guide

hazards.title: Heavy monsoon rain on the coast
hazards.detail: July and August each bring more than 340 millimetres of rain to Puri.

source.title: Puri

hazards.title: Cyclones on the Puri coast
hazards.detail: Cyclone Fani came ashore near Puri on 3 May 2019 with winds of 185 kilometres an hour, felling trees across roads.

source.title: Cyclone Fani

hazards.title: Assaults on visitors at Deomali after dark
hazards.detail: The district posted police and cameras at Deomali in September 2026 after tourists were assaulted; leave the hilltop before evening.

source.title: Trekking restricted after 6 PM as Koraput admin beefs up security at Deomali

gaps: Deomali's height: Wikipedia gives 5,490 feet (1,672 metres); the official Koraput district page gives 5,780 feet (1,762 metres). The Wikipedia figure is recorded.
The text of the Koraput Collector's orders was not found on an official page; only press reports were read. Whether the road to the hilltop has reopened since November 2025 is not known.
No source found for any rule on vehicles on the Puri to Konark coast road through the Balukhand and Konark sanctuary. The official tourism page says nothing on vehicles.
No source found for rules affecting riders at Puri, Konark, Chilika or Gopalpur, or for Odisha helmet rules.
No source found for cyclone months other than the single 2019 event, or for landslides on the ghats between the coast and Koraput.
The highway from the coast up to Koraput was not sourced. Usual number of riding days: no source found.
Videos: the pages give upload dates, not filming dates, so 'filmed' is filled only where the title names a date. Uploads, in order: 2021-09, 2025-07.
